content.comment_body: How will the [product_name] be impacted by the recent Daylight Savings Time changes in the US & Canada? Besides the user-defined settings, will [company_name] release a patch or fix for this?

Hello! The current workaround is to configure your own daylight saving time settings on the [product_name]. Go to Tools/Transfer/Summertime\Wintertime, which is freely customizable (see the checkbox below). This issue is expected to be resolved with the next version of [product_name] ([article_no]). A FAQ will be published soon regarding this topic, and I’ll share it when available. Best regards, [user_name]

Manually entering DST is not an actual fix. DST is based on a day, not a specific date. I'm disappointed with [company_name] after contacting them about this problem. There is no solution for the [article_no] units (which we have many), and the new hardware isn't released yet. This is frustrating.

I agree, this method is a workaround rather than a fix. Could you clarify what you mean by 'day, not a date'? The new DST rules came after the [article_no], so how could it have been supported in that version? You might find help in the following FAQ: [url]. This FAQ is new and will be available in English in a few days. Best regards

DST is determined by a specific day, not a fixed date (for example, spring starts on the second Sunday in March). Using this workaround means you'd need to update the dates annually. Our many [product_name] devices are spread throughout a large city, not just in one location, so updating them every year is time-consuming and costly. I hoped the [product_name] programming software would allow a single update for all devices. I now need programmable controllers that handle DST adjustment properly. I don’t plan to buy more [product_name] units with this same issue. [company_name] had plenty of time to fix this before it became a problem, which is why I’m disappointed.

So, you're looking for a firmware or OS update? In that case, you'd need the [article_no] or a newer version, which isn't available yet, and that's a key difference compared to previous models. Out of curiosity, what would be the situation if you’d used a similar product from Allen Bradley?

You're correct; you’ll need to adjust the settings manually every year, or use the newer hardware when available. Could an external timer work for your application? Best regards and apologies for the inconvenience, [user_name]

Thank you for the suggestions. As far as I know, the latest version isn't available yet. I've discovered another PLC manufacturer whose devices can be programmed for DST based on the day of the month. Changing manufacturers isn't ideal, but I have no choice.
Which manufacturer are you planning to switch to?
Here is the official [company_name] solution: How do you switch between summer and winter time in [product_name] programming software?

analysis.insight_summary: Users indicate that [product_name] hardware from [company_name] does not automatically adjust to the updated Daylight Savings Time rules for the US and Canada. Instead, yearly manual updates are required, which is a burden, particularly for installations across wide areas. There is notable dissatisfaction due to the absence of a firmware upgrade for current devices and the delay in newer hardware availability. Manual approaches are generally considered insufficient for large, distributed systems.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [company_name] hardware and accompanying software to offer automated and reliable DST adjustments according to new regulations, ideally through a software or firmware update for existing devices, without needing to replace hardware.
